Crash of Float Lab returns in the second part of episode 517 of the Joe Rogan Experience, a deeper dive after the first half's groundwork. Float tanks were still a fringe interest when this aired. Rogan's support, and guests like Crash, helped move them toward the mainstream.

The talk goes further into long floats, the mind under zero input, and the craft of building a tank that truly shuts the world out. Crash shares user stories that range from pain relief to strange visions. The entry completes the pair, and together they stand as the show's fullest record on floating.

Jimmy Corsetti and Ben van Kerkwyk team up on ancient mysteries in episode 1928 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Corsetti runs the Bright Insight channel, and van Kerkwyk works with the UnchartedX project studying ancient stone work. Both argue that old sites hold skills history books miss.

The two walk Rogan through precise stone vases, huge blocks, and sites they say defy simple tools. They press their case that a lost, advanced culture left these marks. Rogan asks the hard questions about dating and proof that frame every visit. Atlantis and beyond fill a long, curious talk.

Tucker Carlson and guest Ian Carroll react to the Epstein files in a talk that roams to Pizzagate and a demonic crime web. The title frames the web as global in reach. Carroll is a young researcher with a large online crowd.

The two men work through what the freed files show and what they leave hid. They argue the rot runs past one man to a network with a dark faith of its own. Carlson gives his own take on the evil at the core. Listeners get the full talk in one place. The library holds it as a record of their stated views.
